complexity.correctness_reason: If nums[i] + i exceeds len(nums) - 1, dp[j] is indexed out of range and raises IndexError (e.g. nums = [5] extended to [5, 0] — nums[0]=5 with n=2 gives range(1, 6) and dp[2] fails); NeetCode's cap nums[i] <= 1000 doesn't actually prevent this either — nums = [1000, 0, 0] would index dp[3..1000] — wait, this breaks within NeetCode's own constraints.
complexity.notes: Correct but quadratic: each cell scans up to nums[i] later cells, and the inner range isn't bounded to the array end (harmless, since slices of the range just go out of bounds of dp — actually it would IndexError if... no, range just yields indices beyond len(dp)-1 and dp[j] would raise; in practice nums[i] <= 1000 caps this under NeetCode, but on a generalized input with nums[i] > n this code raises IndexError). An O(n) solution exists via ||a backward scan maintaining the leftmost index that can reach the end (goal post), or equivalently a forward scan tracking the farthest reachable index||.
complexity.summary: Bottom-up DP: dp[i] is True if any index reachable from i (within nums[i] jumps) can itself reach the end; fills the table right to left and returns dp[0].
